## Evidence Intent Extraction — Non-Scoring Calibration

**Source:** LAW-005 | **Locator:** extracted HTML block 1 + extracted HTML block 2 | **SHA256:** 9284e94294ac9d6e565c3186433b2b7b26efb621396d3bc2850cfa654277db3d

---

### Intent D0001
**Locator:** extracted HTML block 1, S00001–S00003; extracted HTML block 2, S00001–S00003
**Factual intent:** The government of Mexico, acting through the Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público (SHCP), issued a formal executive agreement (Acuerdo 173/2022) that established fiscal stimulus percentages, monetary stimulus amounts in pesos per liter, and diminished quotas for the special excise tax on production and services (IEPS) applicable to automotive fuels, for the period December 10–16, 2022.
**Applicable questions:** 5B.1, 5B.3, 6B.1, 6B.2, 6B.3, 8B.1, 8B.2
**Period fit:** Direct evidence for the stated period (December 10–16, 2022); contemporaneous record.
**Limitations:** Document is a procedural administrative issuance; it records the fuel-stimulus schedule but does not independently reveal the policy rationale, welfare incidence, or distributional intent behind the subsidy levels chosen.

---

### Intent D0002
**Locator:** extracted HTML block 2, S00001
**Factual intent:** For the period December 10–16, 2022, the stimulus percentages were: sub-91 octane gasoline 26.96%; premium gasoline (≥91 octanes) and non-fossil fuels 0.00%; diesel 59.77%.
**Applicable questions:** 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.8, 6B.2, 6B.3
**Period fit:** Contemporaneous; explicitly bounded to December 10–16, 2022.
**Limitations:** Percentage alone does not indicate whether the stimulus was actually delivered to end-users, whether it reflected a broader energy or welfare policy, or whether distributional incidence across income classes, regions, or fuel types was assessed.

---

### Intent D0003
**Locator:** extracted HTML block 2, S00003
**Factual intent:** The monetary stimulus amounts (montos del estímulo fiscal) for the period December 10–16, 2022 were: sub-91 octane gasoline $1.4803 pesos/liter; premium gasoline and non-fossil fuels $0.0000 pesos/liter; diesel $3.6071 pesos/liter.
**Applicable questions:** 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.8, 6B.2, 6B.3
**Period fit:** Contemporaneous; bounded to December 10–16, 2022.
**Limitations:** As with D0002, the document records the nominal subsidy amount but not actual budgetary expenditure, pass-through to pump prices, or welfare distribution.

---

### Intent D0004
**Locator:** extracted HTML block 2, S00004–S00005
**Factual intent:** The diminished IEPS quotas (cuotas disminuidas) for the same period were: sub-91 octane gasoline $4.0114 pesos/liter; premium gasoline and non-fossil fuels $4.6375 pesos/liter; diesel $2.4283 pesos/liter.
**Applicable questions:** 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.8, 6B.2, 6B.3
**Period fit:** Contemporaneous; bounded to December 10–16, 2022.
**Limitations:** Same as D0003. The document does not cross-reference the quota levels to pre-existing tax rates or explain the relationship between the quota and the stimulus.

---

### Intent D0005
**Locator:** extracted HTML block 1, S00007; extracted HTML block 2, S00010
**Factual intent:** The complementary stimulus quantities (estímulos complementarios) for the period December 10–16, 2022 were $0.0000 pesos/liter for all fuel categories (sub-91 octane gasoline, premium gasoline/non-fossil fuels, and diesel), meaning no additional complementary stimulus was applied during this period.
**Applicable questions:** 5B.1, 5B.3, 6B.1
**Period fit:** Contemporaneous; bounded to December 10–16, 2022.
**Limitations:** Zero complementary stimulus does not indicate policy intent absent surrounding context; this may reflect routine operation or a gap in supplementary subsidy funding.

---

### Intent D0006
**Locator:** extracted HTML block 1, S00005; extracted HTML block 2, S00008–S00009
**Factual intent:** The formal authority cited for this agreement consists of: (a) the December 27, 2016 Decree establishing IEPS fiscal stimuli for indicated fuels and subsequent modifications, and (b) the March 4, 2022 Decree establishing complementary fiscal stimuli for automotive fuels. Karina Ramírez Arras, Titular de la Unidad de Política de Ingresos No Tributarios of SHCP, issued this agreement as a formal executive-administrative act.
**Applicable questions:** 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.4
**Period fit:** Authority chain dates to 2016 and 2022 decrees; the specific agreement is December 8, 2022 (signed) for the period December 10–16, 2022.
**Limitations:** The document identifies the authorizing decrees but does not independently verify whether those decrees were themselves enacted through constitutionally required legislative processes, whether they had been challenged, or whether the December 2022 administration was the same as the administrations that enacted the foundational decrees.

---

### Intent D0007
**Locator:** extracted HTML block 2, S00007
**Factual intent:** This agreement entered into force the day after its publication in the Diario Oficial de la Federación (Federal Official Gazette), as stated in the sole transitory article.
**Applicable questions:** 8B.1, 8B.2
**Period fit:** Procedural timing provision; entry-into-force date is one day after publication but the specific publication date is not recorded in this segment.
**Limitations:** The actual publication date is not present in the source; temporal alignment with the December 10–16 effectiveness period depends on that missing date.

---

### Intent D0008
**Locator:** extracted HTML block 2, S00008–S00010
**Factual intent:** The agreement was signed in Mexico City on December 8, 2022, by Karina Ramírez Arras, in her capacity as Titular de la Unidad de Política de Ingresos No Tributarios, and in suplencia (in substitution/acting capacity) of the Subsecretario de Hacienda y Crédito Público, as indicated by the signatory block.
**Applicable questions:** 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.4
**Period fit:** Contemporaneous; signed December 8, 2022, for the period December 10–16, 2022.
**Limitations:** The suplencia arrangement means the substantive decision-maker is the Subsecretario; the document does not reveal whether that substitution was routine or contested, or whether the underlying policy was reviewed at a higher ministerial level.

---

**No quotation text reproduced.** All claims are derived from cited segments and are bounded to the factual record within those segments. No score assigned.
